At any rite, the Yunnanese in Canton city (the North bank of the River) (disdained to return the fire.) Some of the rounds are stated to have passed periously close to river slimmers, causing them to leave earlier than usual.
I am informed that several Broadsides were directed at the vicinity of the Police Headquarters in the city but that one volley fell into the Public Park, where there were no soldiers. A number of non-combatants were killed and wounded, so it is stated.

label: paragraph_title
text: Critical Position.

label: paragraph_title
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: The exasperation of the Cantonese at the arrogance of the hired Yuhnanese and Hunanese troops who were brought to Canton by the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen to enable him to oust General Chen (Chiung-ming (Chan Kwing-ming) has led to an outbreak of fighting.

label: text
text: While still protesting loyalty to the principles of Sun Yat-sen and the Kuomintang (Kuomintang) party, the Yunnanese Generals Yang' Hsi-nin (Yang Hsi-man) and Lau Chun-wan have demanded that the authorities order the cessation of troop movements on the East and North Rivef districts; otherwise, they will take measures to resist.

label: text
text: The authorities have replied denouncing their insubordination, dismissing them, and appointing General Chu Pei-teh (Chu Pui-tak) acting Commander of the Yunnanese forces.

label: text
text: This is virtual to a declaration of war. Yang Hsi-nin has seized the Governor's 'yamen', the telephone and telegraph offices, and the electric light plant.

label: text
text: The Yunnanese and Cantonese are entrenched on opposite sides of the Canton River.

label: text
text: The Yunnanese control the whole of the Canton side, while the gunboats under the Canton authorities command the river. The Canton authorities chiefly depend on the Whampon cadets who are trained by Soviet officers.

label: text
text: The foregoing message needs explanation in certain places.

label: text
text:
Explanation in certain places.
It is not the Yunnanese and Hunanese who are ranged against the Cantonese Communists. The Hunanese no longer exist as a fighting force, having been scattered while trying to make their way out of the province of Kwangtung when Dr. Sun was still alive. The Kwangsi merciennaries are the allies of the Yunnanese.

label: text
text: Similarly, General Lau Chun-wan (also spelt Lau Tsun-wan) is not Yunnanese; he commands the Kwangsi army.

label: text
text: Chu Pui-tak also commands a Yunnanese following but he is loyal to the Communists and is their main strength in their stronghold at Honam, the island immediately facing Canton city.

label: text
text: No news has been available from Canton since the time of the night-boats leaving yesterday afternoon as telegraphic communication has been suspended.

label: text
text: This morning, it was gathered that no wireless message had come down from the British gunboats off, Shameen, but that a report had been received to the effect that there had been a general lull in the fighting since yesterday afternoon and up to this morning.

label: text
text: So far, no untoward incident to any foreigner has come to light although those resident in the eastern suburb are inconvenienced through martial law being enforced by the Kwangsi mercenaries and the danger of fighting breaking out there, as the eastern approach is an important strategic point.

label: text
text: There are eight foreign men-of-war at Cantón, viz., the British gunboats, Moth, Tarantula and Cicala, an American sloop and the U.S.S. Pampanga, two French boats and a Japanese man-of-war. Our Canton correspondent reports that General Fan Sheksang, formerly the strong man of Canton, has returned to the city from the West River. Hitherto, the Communists have been counting on his help, or at least his neutrality, but now it is stated

label: text
text: that he has "rejoined his old colleagues:

label: text
text: Mr. Sun Fo (Dr. Sun's son and former Mayor of Canton) went up to Canton as a peacemaker but judging by results, he must have failed. He returned to Hongkong last night.

label: text
text: The Sai On, Kinshan and Paul Beau brought down full complements of refugees last night, the ships being full long before the hour of sailing. As a precaution; the river steamers in Canton had steam up all day yesterday.

label: text
text: The general strike is still in existence and not a cargo boat could be seen in the anchorage yesterday. The river steamers are not carrying any cargo for Canton. This strike is part of the Communist attempt to cut off Canton economically and thus drive the mercenaries out.

label: text
text: Feeling between Cantonese and non-Cantonese in Hongkong ran high on the water-front last night when the river-bonds were leaving for Canton.

label: text
text: Two Yunnanese who were being jostled and threatened by a large crowd, mostly of wharf-coolies were happily taken care of by Mr. W. H. Edmonds of the Public Works Department. Mr. Edmonds was passing in his motor-cycle and saw what was happening. To a "China Mail" reporter, the strangers professed in Southern Mandarin that they were not soldiers but were merchants who had fled from Canton. With two Indian constables bringing up the renr. Mr. Edmonds eventually made a way for the two men who walked behind the motor-cycle and made their way home under Mr. Edmonds's protection.

label: text
text:
(From Our Own Correspondent.)
Carlton, Sunday.

label: text
text: Developments are also reported from the Eastern River and the Canton-Kowloon Railway. The Yunnanese, of course, make out that they have got to grips with General Hsu Shung-chi's. Cantonese vanguards and defeated several hundred of them in the neighbourhood of Shek Pai, a railway station.

label: text
text: I am also informed that the Yunnanese are securing labour for the railway and that their trains will be working.

label: text
text: Interviewed, by the "China Mail" yesterday: a "Cantonese official who has just arrived from Swatow stated that most of General Chan Kwing-ming's former subordinates are joining General Hsu's anti-mercenary army. Their explanation is that Dr. Sun is dead, Chan Kwing-ming is now out of the field, so the Cantonese should unite against the common enemy since the old feud has expired.

label: text
text: General Hsu is reported to be preparing a march on Canton and the danger of a flank or rear attack from pro-Chan forces, has decreased considerably. Commanders Hung Leuk and Yeung Kwan-yu, former subordinates of Chan, are now embodied in Hsu's army. Ngai Bong-ping has returned to the Kuomintang 'fold and has been appointed Defence Commissioner of the West River, stated the official, with the Civil Governorship when the cause is won.

label: paragraph_title
text: LORD CURZON

label: paragraph_title
text: CASTLES FOR THE NATION.

label: text
text: The "Daily Mail" understands that the late Marquis Curzon of Kedleston has left two historic ruins. Tattershall Castle; Lincolnshire, and Bodiam Castle, Sussex, to the nation.

label: text
text: Tattershall Castle, near Withm, is thought to have been erected about 1440. In September, 1911 it was feared that the famous fireplaces would be sent to the United States. They were taken to London, but Lord Curzon, who bought the castle a little later “to save it from being knocked to pieces,” recovered them.

label: text
text: In June 1912 they were returned to their home on decorated lorries which passed beneath triumphal arches. Lord Curzon was in the procession, and his carriage was drawn by ropes by the viliagers.

label: text
text: Bodiam Castle, near Hastings built in 1386, has been described as one of the most beautiful and interesting ruins in England.

label: text
text: It was bought by Lord Curzon in 1917.

label: text
text: The ruins consist of round towers at the angles with five square ones between them, and the great gateway is flanked by two square towers.

label: text
text: An automatic revolver found on a heap of sand at the back of the Kowloon Fire Station was handed over to the Police by Mr. M. Murphy, overseer of the Y.M.C.A, building.

label: text
text: A lamp trimmer on the s.s. On Lee was arrested yesterday for the unlawful possession of 100 tins of opium, one revolver, and 50 rounds of ammunition.

label: paragraph_title
text: SHANGHAI STRIKE.

label: paragraph_title
text:
FRENCH CONCESSION
INVOLVED:

label: paragraph_title
text: NEWSPAPERS' HOPEFUL

label: paragraph_title
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: The strike is spreading to the French Concession. This morning's estimate of the strikers was 250,000, but a number of staffs resumed work today, including the foreign cable companies and Commercial Pressemployees—also 600 workers at the Japanese Dah Koong Mills, and 500 men at the Riverside power station.

label: text
text: The defence is continually being strengthened, approximately 1,500 marines and blue-jackets have been landed from three British, one French, and one Italian cruiser. Seven American destroyers and ten gunboats (British, Japanese and French), in addition to 400 American marines are due to morrow

label: text
text: The absence of riots and the resumption of the workers' indicate that the students are losing their grip of the situation, while the arrival of the Peking Commissioners, whose mission is only to investigate should help to clear the atmosphere.

label: text
text: The wide nature of the student disturbances is further shown by a Hankow message of Friday, which says that 20,000 students are agitating and distributing anti-Foreign leaflets. The Chinese authorities have so far prevented any big demonstrations; the movement began at Hankow on May 25.

label: text
text: Tientsin, June 6.—A party of 1,000 students demonstrated in the Native City yesterday afternoon and this morning. There was no incident; the streets are heavily guarded by police, reinforced by Fengtian soldiers.

label: paragraph_title
text: Tientain Parade

label: text
text: Professors joined the students who made speeches demanding the restoration of Dairen, boycott of the British and abolition of the Concessions.

label: text
text: Marshall Chang Tsc-lin has assured the Police Chief that he will back every effort to maintain order and assume full responsibility in the event of the Peking Government countermanding police measures.

label: paragraph_title
text: Widéspread Agitation

label: paragraph_title
text: PEKING, June 6

label: text
text: Numerous student strikes and demonstrations are reported in many cities throughout the country, but no disorder is reported except at Chinkiang where the police station was wrecked. There were no casualties.

label: text
text: Arrangements are being made to despatch a foreign warship to Chinkiang. Chief Executive Tuan Chi-jui's headquarters have issued a circular telegram to the Provinces, stating that Government has lodged strong protests with the Diplomatic Body as regards the Shanghai shootings; and also sent Messrs. Tsai Ting-kan and Tseng Tsung-chien to Shanghai to investigate.

label: text
text: The telegram advises the merchants and students to attend to their own business and await a settlement.

label: paragraph_title
text: Boycott Urged

label: paragraph_title
text: PEKING; June 6.

label: text
text: The Cabinet met this morning. It is unofficially reported that they decided to issue a mandate somewhat similar in terms to the Chief Executive's circular telegram. The students held a large demonstration at Tienan Men this afternoon, at which they decided to march to the headquarters of the Chamber of Commerce, surround the building and compel the Chamber to carry out an Anglo-Japanese boycott.

label: text
text: The students surrounded the Chamber of Commerce this afternoon, but were refused admission. Finally a party of student delegates were admitted who urged the inauguration of a strike, a boycott and other measures.

label: text
text: The Chamber practically refused their demands but promised to give a further reply tomorrow.

label: paragraph_title
text: Powers' Note.

label: text
text: After a lengthy meeting this morning of the Ministers of the Powers interested, Signor Cerruti (Italian Minister and Doyen of the "Corps Diplomatique") this evening handed the following Note to the Chinese Minister of Foreign Affairs:

label: text
text: I have the honour, in the name of my colleagues and myself, to acknowledge receipt of the Note, dated June 4, which Your Excellency addressed to me, relative to the disorders in Shanghai

label: text
text: While remarking that the reports received by the Chinese Government are incomplete, since they do not mention several attacks against foreigners, my comrades and myself prefer to reserve judgment until the arrival of full details.

label: text
text: To this end, the diplomatic representatives concerned have decided to send a delegation to Shanghai without delay, to study the situation on the spot and submit a report.

label: text
text: I wish at all events, to de-

label: text
text: clare, that the Foreign Authorities of the International Concession, far from having assumed the violent attitude which the Chinese Government attribute to them, have preserved the greatest self-control as proved by the fact that during the past four days—despite numerous provocations—no serious incident has occurred in Shanghai.

label: text
text: I wish to renew the assurance, already given verbally, that the Police of the International Concession have always had instructions to use their arms only if attacked and in imminent danger.

label: paragraph_title
text: Tatsuta" Sails.

label: text
text: The Navy Office states that H.I.J.M.S. "Tatsuta" sailed this afternoon for Shanghai. She carried 200 marines.

label: text
text: Four more destroyers have been despatched to Shanghai from Sascho, while two others have been sent from Formosa to Canton.

label: text
text: PEKING, June 6, 11.48 p.m.

label: text
text: Signor Cerruti (Italian Minister), this afternoon, handed to the Wachiaооц а second Note, in which it was announced that the Powers are sending a delegation to Shanghai on June 8, to investigate and report.

text:

M. S. Tripier, Counsellor of the French Legation.

label: text

Secretary of the Italian Legation.

label: text
text:
The Senior Consul this afternoon replied to the Foreign Commissioner's notes of May 31 and June 1, on the subject of the recent disturbances in Shanghai.
He recapitulated the main facts of the riots, instancing the deliberate attacks on the police, from which it could be seen that the police action was very different to the Commissioner's version. The question of the propriety of the police action is one which should be raised in the course of legal proceedings; when those arrested are tried. There also will be as a matter of course an investigation by the authorities concerned into the action of the police. Besides which competent courts stand ready to deal with any complaints.

label: text
text: The Settlement authorities naturally assume full responsibility for the action taken for the maintenance of order, but remind the Commissioner of the grave responsibility of the local Chinese authorities in respect to anti-foreign agitation, conducted beyond the limits of the Settlement, to which these regrettable occurrences may largely be attributed.

label: paragraph_title
text: Chinkiang Outbreak

label: text
text: The British Consul-General at Chinkiang, near Nanking, tele-graphed to-day: There are riots

label: text
text: in the Concession; can the Navy send assistance?" To which the following reply was sent: "American Admiral last evening wirelessed to an American warship, proceeding up river to put in at Chinkiang."

label: text
text: Later messages stated that the situation was serious. Rioting students had wrecked three houses in the Concession, the Chinese Police, told off-protect foreigners, proving absolutely useless. The rioters carried on joyfully until the Commanding Chinese brought his own troops to the scene, four hours after the Consul General had asked for assistance.

label: text
text: The General restored order and the foreign women and children returned ashore from the boats on which they had taken refuge but a message to night says that the situation is again serious.

label: text
text: The U.S.S. Paul Jones is now due at Chlnkiang and H.M.S. Woodlark should reach there on Monday.

label: paragraph_title
text: Home Labour Views

label: paragraph_title
text: LONDON, June 7

label: text
text: The Council of the Independent Labour Party has issued a statement, sympathising with the alleged oppressive conditions introduced by foreign capitalism into the Far East. It asserts that under the British Flag in the Foreign Concession at Shanghai children of five years of age and upwards are working night and day shifts of twelve hours for seven days weekly, for twopence a day.

label: text
text: The Labourites demand the immediate application of labour legislation worthy of European standards; also the withdrawal of armed forces. The Council protests against the foreign occupation of Chinese cities.

label: text
text:
LONDON, June 7.
Discussing the trouble in the Far East, the "Observer" says that China cannot long be denied fiscal

label: text
text: autonomy, which is already enjoyed by India. A general re-adjustment in the relationship between the

label: text
text: Western Powers and China is imperative.

label: text
text: China is no more proof against the contagion of her national consciousness and self-respect than the other great countries of the East. The task of the Powers is to give the new spirit it's direction and outlet.

label: paragraph_title
text: End in Sight?

label: text
text: The morning papers think that the end of the strike is within sight. There is certainly a remarkable change in the general atmosphere. The Chinese in the streets are beginning to fraternise with the Volunteers.

label: text
text: This is mainly due to the impending departure from Peking of diplomatic representatives, which will lead to the discussions by which the Chinese invariably expect to settle troubles big and small, when momentary excitement has passed.

label: text
text: The situation is still very delicate; however, and little would be required to revive the fires of racial antagonism which the extremists are continually fanning. An outstanding feature of the riots has been the loyalty to the Municipal Council of the Chinese Volunteers, despite the bitter attacks of the vernacular papers, while only 100 out of 1,600 Chinese police failed to withstand the strain of the continual viuperation heaped on them at every point by the strikers.

label: text
text: The arrival at Chinkiang of the U.S.S. Paul Jones last night synchronized with the abatement of the riots, which will apparently not be renewed.

label: text
text: To day's reports state that the situation is quiet. A short wireless message says that students are working up a strike at Kiukiang. There are no details.

label: text
text: That the local student situation is outwardly quiet is largely due to the Tupan of Hsiao-yaonan to day issuing two proclamations, the first to the Chinese and foreign citizens of Wuhan and the second to the educational commissioner and the police. He directed the maintenance of peace. The commissioner also issued a proclamation to the students to the same effect.

label: paragraph_title
text: Peking Mandate

label: paragraph_title
text: PEKING, June 7.

label: text
text: The Government issued a mandate last night stating that patriotic citizens had attempted to demonstrate at Shanghai and some had been killed and others wounded, at which the Chief Executive was greatly afflicted. He had asked the Waichiaopu to protest strongly, and had sent delegates of high standing to Shanghai to carry out negotiations to find who was responsible. The Government always protects the interests of the people. All must follow the right channels and work together at this time of difficulty.

label: text
text: The students did not obtain much satisfaction at the Chamber of Commerce yesterday evening, so they proceeded to the Bankers' Association, where they only found one secretary.

label: text
text: They made the usual demands for a boycott etc., and also demand-ed that funds be sent to assist the Shanghai strikers.

label: text
text: The Bankers' Association are meeting to-morrow to consider the demands. Things were very quiet to-day and there were no demonstrations.

label: paragraph_title
text: Further Peking Note.

label: paragraph_title
text: (Courtesy of the Daily Bulletin.)

label: text
text: I had the honour to address to Your Excellency on the 1st inst. Note in which I begged you to give urgent necessary instructions to the Consular authorities at Shanghai to immediately free those persons who had been arrested and to act in concert with the Special Commissioner for Foreign Affairs, there to hinder the eventual return of similar cases.

label: text
text: The following is a translation of another Note sent by the Wachiaopu to the Italian Minister, M. Cerruti, as Senior Minister of the Interested. Powers, this evening, "concerning the bloody affair at Shanghai":

label: text
text: Contrary to my expectation, new reports of an inauspicious character continue to reach me, according to which the police of the International Settlement on the 1st inst. again fired on the people, of whom three were killed and eighteen wounded, whilst the persons arrested have not all been freed. Other reports state that most of the victims were shot in the back without any agents of the police having been killed or wounded, which proves that the shooting was quite unjustified.

label: text
text: The violent attitude of the authorities of the International Concession, which has excited the discontent of the general public, creates the gravest consequences, notably the declaration of strikes by the merchants and workers in Shanghai.

label: text
text: The death sentence on Madame Nicolava in connection with the bomb outrage in the cathedral has been commuted to "light seclusion for life."

label: text
text: Peking, June 6.—Students all over the country are organising strikes and demonstrations but the only disorder is in Chinkiang, where the Police Station was wrecked without casualties. A foreign warship is being despatched thither. Professors have joined in the demonstration at Tientsin, where speeches were made demanding the restoration of Dairen, an anti-British boycott and abolition of concessions.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: LUCKY ARREST:

label: paragraph_title
text: ARMED ROBBERY FOILED. SMART WORK.

label: text
text: A Chinese constable attached No. 7 Police Station (West Point effected a smart arrest on Friday night and thus foiled the well-law plans of a gang of men to rob Chinese house at the junction of Sassoon Road and Pokfulam Road. The raid was timed to take place after the street traffic had stopped. The movements of one member the gang, who was on his way, meet his confederates, called investigation from the constable patrol duty, and a search result in a dagger and some wire bear found on him. The arrested ms subsequently made a statement the police in which he alleged the the dagger was given to him by other man and that they were go to Pokfulam to commit an arn robbery. Soon afterwards the others were also arrested.

label: text
text: The same night another Club was arrested at Queen's Road TV following the discovery of a dog hidden in his shoe. This man made an admission to the Ed that he was proceeding on an awful mission.

label: text
text: The two principal figures these arrests are being charged the Central Magistracy by R sional Inspector Peter Grant.
